cases.name: uses print() rather than just writing text

exercise1.hint: Put your message inside print(), with the text in quotes: print("your message here").

cases.name: uses a separate print() for each line

exercise2.hint: Each line needs its own print() on its own line. Three lines of output means three print() statements.

questions.prompt: A script contains print("Ready"). After you run it, where should you look for Ready?
choices: In the terminal or output panel used to run the script
In a new file named Ready
Inside the source file, replacing the print call
questions.explain: print sends text to standard output, which this site shows in the editor output panel. It does not save a file or modify the source code.

questions.prompt: Which of these will cause an error?
questions.explain: Without quotes, Python reads Hello as a variable name, and no variable by that name exists.

questions.prompt: How many lines does print("a")\nprint("b") produce?
questions.explain: Each print() ends with a newline, so each call starts its output on a fresh line.

questions.prompt: Why do single and double quotes both work for strings?
choices: Python accepts either, so you can use the other kind inside without escaping
questions.explain: Having both means you can write "it's fine" or 'she said "hi"' without escaping anything.

questions.prompt: Match each idea to its meaning.
right: Enclose the arguments of a function call
Mark the start and end of text
questions.hint: Identify the text, the values passed to print, and the punctuation that separates those values.
questions.explain: Quotes: Mark the start and end of text. Comma in print: Separates values passed to print. Parentheses: Enclose the arguments of a function call.

questions.prompt: Arrange these steps in the intended order.
items: Display the result in the output
questions.hint: Find the first step that does not depend on any earlier result. Then follow each dependency.
questions.explain: An argument expression must have a value before the function can use it.

questions.label: Predict the first line of output (without surrounding quotes).
questions.prompt:
print("Score:", 4 + 5)
print("Next level")

First output line: ___
questions.hint: Trace each line in order and write down the current values. Stop at the first print call.
questions.explain: Python evaluates 4 + 5 to 9, then print receives the text Score: and the number 9. The second call starts on a new line because the first call ended its line.

reflection-ex3.hint: Describe what you actually did: what the file was called, how you ran it, and where the output appeared.
